elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: § 8.2 as rendered retains automatic renewal ("Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives sixty days' advance written notice") with no mutual-written-agreement alternative, and the conditional auto-renewal elements are not all satisfied (opt-out is 60 days, not ≤30; no Vendor reminder). To reach preferred, either require renewal by mutual written agreement or cure the 30-day opt-out and 60-day reminder limbs.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: § 8.2: "Each Order Form renews for twelve months" — renewal term is exactly 12 months.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: § 8.2 as rendered requires "sixty days' advance written notice" — exceeds the 30-day preferred maximum. Operative fix would be to state thirty days.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder mechanic anywhere in §§ 8.2–8.3; § 8.3's 90-day notice relates only to a Fee increase, not to the fact of renewal. A separate Vendor renewal-reminder obligation would have to be inserted.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: § 8.3 (retained unchanged): "Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent."

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 8.2 shortens the window from "one hundred eighty days" to "sixty days' advance written notice" — exactly the 60-day fallback maximum. The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a numeral-matching artefact: the figure is spelled out in words consistent with the drafting convention of the surrounding clause, and substantively equals 60 days.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: § 8.3 caps renewal uplift at "the lesser of" CPI and "three percent", which is stricter than the 5 percent fallback ceiling; no change needed.

reasons: The fallback checklist is complete: the notice window is now 60 days (element 1) and the pre-existing CPI/3% cap already beats the 5% ceiling (element 2), so the position is complete at the fallback level.

The single deterministic failure ("non-renewal notice window ≤ 60 days — number not found") is a false negative caused by the number being spelled as "sixty" rather than "60"; the operative text reads "sixty days' advance written notice", which is 60 days and matches the word-form numbering used throughout §§ 8.2–8.3.

Preferred remains unmet on three limbs: no mutual-written-agreement default, opt-out at 60 rather than 30 days, and no Vendor reminder at least 60 days before renewal. These are correctly treated as preferred-only sub-elements noted in the rationale.

Minimality holds: the only textual change is "one hundred eighty" → "sixty" in § 8.2. Favourable retained language (12-month term, mutuality of the notice right, § 8.3's CPI/3% cap, 90-day increase notice, no uplift on prepaid periods) is untouched, and no extras, survival tails, or procedures were added.

Intent is preserved: the renewal term, fee-increase mechanics, notice-of-increase timing, and prepaid-period protection all survive without contradiction; no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling.
The "deviation" classification is correct because the original 180-day window failed the 60-day fallback and sat in walk-away territory (>90 days), justifying a redline.
